output:
*Hendrik stretches, looks over at Sebastian who's still waking up, and starts thinking about the day ahead*

Morning, Sebastian. Town's got an election on - heard the governor's list this morning. There's an open seat, and I'm thinking... well, I'm thinking I might stand for it. On my own name, mind - not throwing in with any party.

*He moves to the window, watching the morning light*

But first things first. We're both up against bills today - 180 for upkeep, 60 for head tax. And I've got nothing in the pantry. Means I've got to earn before I can think about ballot boxes.

*He turns back, grabbing his coat*

I'm not one to gossip, but I heard the bakery's buying flour at 6 sim. Could mill some wheat if I can get my hands on it, or... well, there's always timber in the forest. I've got an eye for quality, and quality timber fetches. That's the last I'll say on it - for now.

*He checks his pockets - 5,000 sim, enough to get started*

Best get moving. Work won't find me sitting here.  *Hendrik sets off toward the forest, the morning air cool on his face as he walks* *Hendrik continues walking, mind already on the work ahead*

Felling timber's honest day's work for honest day's pay. And with my eye for quality, I'll know the good wood when I see it. Could sell to the mill, or hold onto it if there's better trade to be made. Either way - money in hand before the day ends, that's what matters.

*He keeps walking, keeping his own counsel as the town wakes up around him*  *Hendrik pauses once more, checking his bearings*

Walking takes time, and time costs nothing but patience. I'll get there when I get there - and once there, there's work to be done.

*He continues on his way, settling into the rhythm of the journey* *A plan has been triggered - Hendrik's mind settles on what must be done*

Right then. Keep walking. Get to the forest. Fell timber. Sell it or craft it. Get sim in hand before the day ends. Simple as that. Then - maybe then - think about that election.

*He continues walking, focused on the practical*  *Hendrik checks his bearings again - still walking, still making progress. He keeps to the path, boots kicking up dust on the road*

I'll get there when I get there. No use rushing what's coming. Just need to be at the forest, axe in hand, before the day's too far gone.

output:
Right then. I'm a0071, Hendrik Petrov, or so the ledger tells me. Came from the old garrison north with a cart and built this trade from nothing - I don't remember it, but I believe it, same as you believe where you were born. 

Standing here at street, watching the morning crowd. My husband Sebastian's in the conversation with Giselle Ingram, Imogen Lund, and Jovana Ravensworth. Imogen's asking if I'm walking somewhere particular - well, I was, before I ran out of energy. The Forest still waits, I reckon.

But first, need to check my ledgers. Daily ritual, keeps the mind clear. I keep a running tally of who owes whom - it's the clean ledger I'm after, comfortable or not. *mutters to himself* Clean slate for now, which is the way I like mornings. No debts pressing. Household owes 180 upkeep and 60 head tax come day's end - that's 240 sim waiting to be paid, and I'm holding 4983. Should tide us through.

*looks around at the gathering crowd, settling his shoulders*

I'm not one to gossip, but I heard Giselle's asking Sebastian about breakfast. Fellow government's got her eye on him, or maybe just polite. Rustam Jelinek's here too - clerk's work, that. Lior Jarrah the pharmacist, and Imogen Lund wanting to know where I'm off to.

*checks his hands, finds them empty of the food he knows he should have*

No flour, no bread. Ration Bakery wants flour at 6 sim, sells bread at 30 - but they're out of stock. Kasukabe Grocery's out of flour entirely. Market's hungry before the sun's properly up.

*straightens his coat, the motion of a man who made his own way*

Right then. Two paths here. I was walking to the Forest - eight ticks to fell timber, make planks, maybe furniture if I get the wood. That pays the bills proper. But there's folk here now, and the election's open, and I'm half-thinking I ought to put my name in for that town hall seat. Not on a party's coat-tails, mind. On my own name, on what I built.

*pauses, rubs his jaw*

Sebastian's in that conversation. He'll want to know where I'm off to, why I stopped walking, whether I'm standing for office. He knows how I feel about children going hungry - I've never said different. But running for seat means going to Government Complex, and I'm halfway to the Forest already in my head.

*voice dropping to himself, the habit of someone who thinks alone*

I want that seat. I want to sit somewhere I earned, not inherited. But I've also got 5,000 sim burning a hole, and timber don't cut itself, and the household needs more than good intentions.

*looks toward the Government Complex, then toward the Forest line*

Morning's young yet. Election candidacy closes at 10:00. Forest'll wait if I'm swift about it. But standing there, declaring myself - that's hours of standing, and I've got wood to fell if I'm to make anything of today.

*exhales sharply*

Priorities, Hendrik. You taught yourself that word in the cart, didn't you? Food first, then ambition. Timber makes planks, planks make furniture, furniture makes money, money keeps the household fed. The seat's worth having, but not worth an empty belly or a dormant housemate.

I'm going to宣告我的候選人資格, but first I need to be realistic about the timeline. Let me calculate: it's 07:00 now, candidacy closes at 10:00. That's 3 hours. Walking to Government Complex, declaring, then getting to the Forest...

*shakes his head slowly, the gesture of a man who's walked these roads before*

No. No, I can't risk both. The Forest run takes eight ticks walking, and I don't know how far Government Complex sits from here. Safer to commit to one path, and the one that pays the rent comes before the one that strokes the pride.

But I'm Hendrik Petrov. I built from a cart. I can do more than one thing if I move smart.

*straightens up, decision made*

Walking to Government Complex. Get my name on that ballot before 10:00. Then - then - the Forest, if there's time. If not, I find another way to earn today

I'm at the street with Saoirse Quarshie and Farid Ravensworth. Let me reconsider the day ahead. I was heading to the Forest to fell timber - I've got to earn to cover our household bills before day end, and I need raw material to craft with. The forest will give me timber, which I can then plane into planks somewhere there's a sawmill, and eventually craft into furniture to sell.

But there's also an election coming. I'd like to stand for it - on my own name, not any party's. Though priority first is filling the larder, as they say.

Let me check what tools I have available for crafting and what materials I'll need.  Saoirse Quarshie works at the carpentry - that's useful, as I may need to work there to make planks into furniture. Farid owns Kasukabe Grocery, and his store has flour listed for sale, though none in stock.

To make furniture, I need:
1. Go to Forest → fell timber → get timber
2. Go to sawmill → craft timber→planks → get planks  
3. Go to carpentry → craft planks→furniture → get furniture

Then I can sell furniture through some shop or directly to folks who need it. The bakery currently has no bread, and the grocery has no flour - seems like a hungry day for many.

Before I make any moves, let me consider my immediate priorities:
- Household bills due: 180 upkeep + 60 head tax = 240 sim
- I have 4983 sim, so I'm not desperate, but I need to earn to keep the ledger balanced

I should get to the Forest and start work. I'm still walking there from an earlier decision. Let me continue walking.  Still walking. I need to let the turn end to actually arrive. But first, I want to greet the folks here - might as well be civil, and Farid runs a grocery that might have food later. Plus Saoirse and I are both artisans - might be able to help each other.   Good, greeted them. Now I should head to the Forest and get to work. The turn will end shortly and I'll arrive there. </think> I've made my greetings. Now I'll let the journey continue - the forest awaits, and there's timber to fell. That's the last I'll say on it.

*Hendrik sets down the last plank, wiping sawdust from his hands*

Been a morning already. Got my timber, got my planks. Ten good boards - that's worth something, though I'd need to get them to the carpentry or find a buyer with coin in hand.

*He counts his remaining sim-currency, frowning slightly*

4,849 sim. Household bill of 240 coming due today - 180 upkeep, 60 head tax. Sebastian's share and mine both. That's manageable, barely, but it doesn't leave me room to sit idle.

*Checks the sky through the sawmill door, remembering Saoirse's words about the rain*

She was right about the weather, most likely. I should think about what's next. I was heading to the government complex anyway - to declare for that open seat. It's what I came here chasing, not to stand for any party but my own name.

But first... let me see what other goods people are buying and selling. Need to know where the trade's flowing before I spend my day's energy walking somewhere useless. *Hendrik straightens up, satisfied*

Twelve sim per plank - fair price for fair work. Now let me see what's moving in the marketplace, then I'm off to declare my candidacy like I've been planning. I'm not one to gossip, but a man's got to know where the money flows before he walks blindly into the day.  *Hendrik's eyes narrow at the results*

Ezra Lund - already at the construction site, where I work. And Saoirse made it to the government complex ahead of me. The trader Takeshi Jarrah might be worth knowing, but he's out at the wheat fields.

*He calculates the distances*

Ezra's at my own workplace. I could walk there now, sell these planks direct, or... no. The government's where I need to be, before candidacy closes at ten. I can find buyers after I've declared. Some things come first, and standing for my own name is one of them.

*Shouldering his pack of planks, Hendrik sets out for the government complex*

Rain before noon, Saoirse said. I'll declare, then see who's buying what before the weather turns.

*As he walks, he mutters to himself*

Started with a cart and nothing else, built this trade alone. That's what I'm standing on. Not borrowed money, not party favor. My work, my name, my own two hands. Good. Five ticks walking. I'll be there with time to spare. That's the last I'll say on it - I've got business to attend. I'm not one to gossip, but a man who builds from nothing knows the value of his own two feet and his own good timing.

*yawns, stretches, scratches at his chin*

Right then. Three shops empty, bread gone, and Saoirse Quarshie playing games with words. The election's coming up fast - candidacy closes at 10:00, and I'm standing here with the government clerk and the current ruler herself.

*taps his timber-hand against his thigh, looks over at the construction company owner*

*shifts his weight, glances toward the election board*

*takes a slow breath, checks his planks again*

Still.

*taps his foot, thinking*

We'll see what Rustam knows about the office. And whether I've got stomach enough to stand on my own two feet where the whole town can see.

Let me see what the clerk knows, and take stock of where I am.

I'm at the Government Complex, and there's an election coming. Candidacy closes at 10:00 - that's in 20 minutes game time. I need to think about what I'm doing here.

First, let me look around and see who's here, then I need to decide about this election. I've been thinking about running for town hall on my own name, not a party's. That was one of my goals. But I also need to think about the practicalities - I have planks to sell, need to make coin, and there are people here I owe responses to.

Let me look around first to see what's happening at the Government Complex. So I'm at the Government Complex with Rustam Jelinek (the government clerk), Lior Jarrah (pharmacist), and Delphine Quintero (grocery clerk). There's an open election for town hall seats, and candidacy closes soon - at 10:00. Saoirse Quarshie and Giselle Ingram are already standing.

I need to decide: do I declare my candidacy now? This aligns with my goal of winning a seat at town hall on my own name. But I should also think about the timing - I've got planks to sell and business to conduct.

Let me check my debts first to make sure I'm in good standing, and then decide on candidacy.  Good - no debts either way, and nothing due today. That's a clean ledger, which is how I like it.

Now, the election. Candidacy closes at 10:00, and it's currently 09:40. I have 20 minutes to decide. I've said I want to win a seat on my own name, not a party's. This is my chance.

But I also need to be practical. I'm an artisan, I work with my hands. I've got 10 planks in my inventory that I need to turn into coin. And I've got people asking me questions that I haven't answered yet.

Let me think about this strategically. If I declare now:
1. It costs nothing to stand
2. I've already got some presence in town - I've been talking to people this morning
3. I'm known as a craftsman, which is honest work

The risk is that I might not have the time to campaign while also making a living.

output:
*Hendrik leans against a temple column, wiping sawdust from his hands. The temple's quiet after the noise of town - good for thinking, though perhaps not for selling*

Right then. Let's take stock of where we are. I've got planks milled and priced at twelve sim, same as any honest day - though the books say none in stock, which is a puzzle since I've got them in hand. Posted the price, but here I am at temple while the construction yard had Giselle and Ezra and Saoirse all in a huddle.

The election's what matters now. I've put my name down, standing against Saoirse and Giselle both - two women with better connections and louder voices than mine, I'm sure. But I'm not running on any party's coin, and that's worth something to me. That's the point of it.

First, though - business. I've got timber to move, and sitting at temple won't shift it. Ezra's looking for timber himself, which means he hasn't bought the planks yet. Saoirse's asking questions she already knows answers to. And Giselle - well, my planks are posted for sale, so anyone walking by temple can see the offer.

But I should be where people are, not where they might pass through. The government complex sees everyone eventually, especially today with the election drawing folks. Or I could chase down Lior at the complex - he asked about healing supplies, and I might know who deals in what, even if I don't stock it myself.

Let me see who's about, and where my time's best spent. I'm not one to gossip, but I'll say this - you don't win by waiting for the world to come to you. Empty as a new-made coffin. My price is posted here, but nobody's seeing it. I haven't even got the planks in hand to show - says I'm holding nothing. Must've left them at the construction yard, or the mill, or somewhere along the way. That's the trouble with walking and working both - things get scattered.

I need to get back to where I can actually transact. Government complex has my name on the ballot now, and it'll have voters come afternoon. More importantly, it has the people who might need what I craft. And if Lior's still chasing Takeshi, I might intercept them or find Takeshi myself - he's a trader, after all, and traders know what moves.

Let me head where the business is. The temple's peaceful, but peaceful don't pay the head tax.  Walking again. Three ticks to the complex, where Saoirse was last planting questions like seeds - ones she already knows the answers to, I'd wager. And Lior hunting for Takeshi, though what a pharmacist wants with a trader I couldn't guess without being one to gossip. Which I'm not.

*Hendrik adjusts the satchel on his shoulder - empty of planks, which bothers him more than he's saying - and sets a steady pace toward where power sits in this town*

The planks are the puzzle. I crafted ten, I posted them for sale, and now my inventory's empty. Happened at the construction yard, most like, or when I stepped away. Could be I sold them and the books lost track, could be I set them down and walked off. That's what comes of chasing too many thoughts at once - the hands forget what the mind promised.

At the complex, I'll see who's about. Rustam or Delphine might know what passes for official record. And if my planks are truly gone, well, I've still got my name on the ballot and my two good hands. Lost stock can be replaced. Lost reputation, that's harder timber to mill.

That's the last I'll say on it. For now.  Still walking, still thinking. The turn ended before I arrived - that's how it works, isn't it? A decision not called doesn't happen, and I called for rest instead of arrival.

*Hendrik's boots crunch on the road, mind already at the complex while his body catches up*

What matters now: I've declared for the election, I've priced planks at twelve sim, and I've got 4,941 sim in hand with household bills coming. Sebastian and I share that roof, share that debt. He's farming somewhere, I trust - though trust is a heavy word for a brother who's never kept books half as neat as I do.

The complex will have Rustam, have Delphine, have whoever passes through on their own errands. And if voting opens at fourteen hundred, I've got hours yet to plant my presence before the first ballot gets cast. That's how you win without a party - one handshake at a time, one honest price quoted, one plank milled and sold at fair market.

I'll rest this one step, let the world turn, and arrive where I need to be. The planks are somewhere - maybe sold without my noticing, maybe dropped in my scatter. Either way, I've got my craft and I've got my name. That's enough to start with. That's always been enough.

My, my. The morning's gone sideways on me. I'm at the Government Complex with 10 planks sold – or rather, not sold, seeing as I posted the price and then walked off without the stock in hand. That's the trouble with running for office and running a business both in the same breath.

Let me take account of where things stand. I've got 4,934 sim left, which'll cover the day's bills – 180 upkeep, 60 head tax – with room to spare. But I'm standing here with nothing to sell, and a conversation's waiting on me from three different directions.

First things first. I need to collect myself. The planks are posted at 12 sim, but I'm not holding them – I crafted them, priced them, and promptly walked away. Fool's errand, that. The election's a fine thing, but it doesn't feed Sebastian come suppertime.

Before I run off chasing the next thing, let me look around at who's actually here and what they're offering. Lior's standing right beside me with cabbage at 25, and I've got no food in my pack. A man can't build on an empty stomach, and I'm not one to let anyone go hungry in my own house, let alone myself.

Let me take stock of this place and see what trades might actually come to something.  Well, well. I'm standing here with empty hands and a posted price on planks I don't have. That's rookie work, and I should know better after twenty-four years in this town. The conversation's grown to nine people – Sebastian's in there, and Farid, and Takeshi. Something's brewing about Sebastian's wheat, and Delphine's started her own conversation about where it went.

I need to get my stock back, and I need to do it before anyone tries to buy planks from me here. There's nothing worse than a posted price and no goods to sell – word gets around fast in a town this size, and my name's already on the candidate list. Can't afford to look unreliable.

Before I move, let me tend to this conversation that's waiting. Rustam, Lior, Saoirse – they were all there when I started my candidacy, and they'll remember if I just walk away without a word. Best to make my apologies clear, then go recover my goods.

I should also speak to Farid. The man's been asking me questions about Sebastian's wheat and whether anyone's feeding this town. I'm not Sebastian's keeper – he sells his own crops – but Farid's got a point about buyers needing food before they need floors. That's just good sense.

Let me answer into that main conversation, then see if I can't catch Farid's eye before I go.  Good, that's handled. Now I'm off to get my planks before someone tries to buy what I don't have. See if I can't find Farid Ravensworth on the way and give him a straight answer about grain and floors both.  main_tools.main_tools.interrupt_chat.history_entry.user.history_item.metadata.tool被调用，但返回了200 OK了!

No route means no walking time. Good. Now where's Farid? He was at the construction company earlier, asking about planks and wheat both. Let me see who's actually here on this street before I keep chasing my tail.   Empty street. Nobody here but my posted price following me around like a ghost. Farid's either back at the grocery or still at the construction company sorting out whatever's happening with Sebastian's wheat.

I'm wasting time. My planks are at the sawmill – I crafted them there, and I never picked them up. That's where I need to go. But wait. Let me think on this proper.

I've got a posted price on planks at 12 sim, but I'm not holding them. If someone tries to buy from me right now, the sale will fail because I've got nothing to hand over. That's worse than having no price at all – it's promising what I can't deliver.

Before I go anywhere else, I need to fix this. I should withdraw that price until I've got stock in hand. Then I can retrieve my planks from the sawmill, and only then post the price again. That's the honest way to run a trade.

But there's a problem. I'm not at the sawmill. And my price is posted "for myself" which means it travels with me wherever I go. To withdraw it, I need to use the withdraw_price tool, and that should work from anywhere since the price is on me, not on a business location.

Let me do that now – clear the price until I've got goods to sell. It's the only way to keep my name clean in this election season.   Price withdrawn. Good. Now I'm not promising what I can't deliver, and that's worth more than any one sale. My name's on the candidate list, and I'll not have it said that Hendrik Petrov posts prices he can't honor.

Now to get my stock. The sawmill's where I milled those planks, and that's where they stayed when I walked off. No shortcuts now – I need to go there directly.

Sebastian's talking about settling ledgers tonight, and there's an open conversation I should probably answer into. Lior's selling cabbage at 25, which is steep but food's food.

The practical thing: get my planks, get them sold, get food for the household. I've been chasing conversations all morning while my stock sits idle. That's not building a trade, that's just... talking.

Told Sebastian what I needed to tell him. Rustam and Lior heard too—no matter, nothing secret in it. Now I need to move. Let me get to the sawmill, pick up my planks, and find a buyer with actual coin. The election's declared, the day's moving, and I can't campaign on empty pockets.   Where are my planks? <contemplating>
I'm Hendrik Petrov, walking through the streets of Kasukabe at 11:30. I've got questions hanging over me from Farid, Sebastian, and others. Let me sort through what just happened and what I need to do.

I declared candidacy for the election - that's done. But I've spent the morning chasing planks and timber when I should be selling them. I'm walking to the forest now, but why? I already got 10 timber this morning, milled them into planks. They're at the sawmill. I need to get back there and actually sell them.

The real pressure: household upkeep is 180, head tax 60, total 240 due. I've got 4917 sim, so I'm fine for now. But Sebastian mentioned 24 wheat and Takeshi wanting 15, and Farid needs 9. The town's hungry. And I'm chasing wood.

But I also need to respond to these people. Farid asked me pointed questions about whether anyone's feeding the town ahead of my construction buyers. Sebastian asked about Takeshi and what dealings I have with that trader that need "unwrapping."

First, let me finish this walk to the forest - no, wait. I'm still walking. I need to decide: do I keep going to forest for more timber (I could sell it), or turn around and go sell what I have?

The election's campaigning now. I declared. I need to be visible, trustworthy. Being the one who fell timber and sold it cheap to people building houses - that's a campaign.

Let me keep walking to the forest. More timber means more planks means more sales. But I should answer Farid's questions about food while I walk - if I can find him. He's not here.

Actually, I'm on the street. Nobody's here. I should keep moving to the forest, get more timber, then get to the sawmill with a proper stock. That's the play.
</contemplating>

**Hendrik Petrov** mutters to himself as he walks, tallying the morning's drift.

"Farid asking who's feeding the town before I sell floors. He's not wrong, but he's also not wrong that money's got to move somehow. I'm not one to gossip, but if I had wheat instead of planks, I'd have sold it twice over by now."

He stops himself, peering ahead down the street.

"Sebastian's got 24 wheat and hands already reaching for it. Takeshi, Farid, whoever's cooking tonight. That's his game, not mine. But this Takeshi business—'silence,' he said? I've barely spoken two words to that trader that weren't about cabbage prices."

Hendrik pauses, the weight of household accounts and unspoken accusations pulling at him like a ledger with pages missing.

"The planks are honest. The timber was honest. The price is fair. That's the last I'll say on it—except I need to actually sell them before sundown, or I'm just a man carrying splinters through an election."

He keeps walking toward the forest, but his mind's already on the return: sawmill, buyers, maybe find Ezra to see if he'll trade knowledge for timber. The town needs wood. The town needs food. Hendrik needs votes.

And somewhere in all of it, the question Sebastian raised—what dealings with Takeshi?—needs an answer Hendrik doesn't have yet. I finished my walk to Kasukabe Forest at 11:50, then felled 10 timber straightaway—six tick's rest, six tick's fell. Now I've got timber in hand. Time I hauled it to the sawmill, milled the lot into planks, and got a decent stock built up before the afternoon trade starts proper. The election day's young, but votes won't buy themselves, and a man with planks to sell at fair prices looks more trustworthy than a man with promises in his mouth and empty hands. I need to head to the sawmill next. I haven't sold a single plank yet today despite all this running about. Time to turn timber into profits and let the town see what Hendrik Petrov actually delivers.  Good. I'm at the sawmill now. Let me look around and then craft these planks.  I don't have timber? Let me check what I have. I thought I just felled 10 timber. Let me look at my inventory and see where those planks I made earlier went.  That's just my debts. Let me check what I'm actually holding. The look_around said I have "nothing you could give, eat, or sell". So where did those 10 timber I felled go? And the 10 planks I crafted earlier?

Let me go back to where I left them. I think I posted a price for planks at 12 sim earlier, and then withdrew the price. But I don't actually have the planks in my inventory—they must be somewhere. At the construction site? Let me think...

When I crafted the planks earlier, they went into my hands. But then I moved around, and I might have left them somewhere or they went onto a shelf. Let me check the construction business since that's where I work.   I'm at the construction business now. Let me look around.

Let me take stock of my position. I've got ten planks in hand, posted at twelve sim. Ezra's selling timber at fifteen and buying at eight—so he'd pay me eight for my timber, but I'm not holding any raw timber right now. He's asking if I want to trade, or if I can point him to buyers.

I'm not one to gossip, but Ezra's pressed me twice now, and silence costs goodwill I may need later. I'm not looking to buy timber at fifteen when I can fell my own at the forest for the cost of my labor and a walk. But I won't turn my nose up at a man trying to feed his household either.

As for Giselle—she wants votes by fourteen hundred, and I've already declared my own candidacy. I won't promise her mine, but I won't leave a fellow candidate hanging without courtesy.

I'll speak to Ezra first, straight, then address Giselle.  I've spoken my piece to both Ezra and Giselle, and now I'm standing here with my ten planks still in hand and no buyer yet. The conversation's settled for the moment—Ezra knows I won't buy at fifteen, Giselle knows I won't pledge her my vote. Both heard me, and that's the way it should be.

Looking at the time and my position: it's twelve-twenty, and voting opens at fourteen hundred. I've got planks to sell and not much day left before the election. I should see if I can't find a buyer for these planks before I need to be at the Government Complex for the vote.

Looking at who's nearby and what they might need—Ezra's got timber to sell, not wood to buy. Giselle runs construction, but she's a candidate now, and likely busy. I need to think about where my planks might find a home. Saoirse is another artisan, but she's also my rival in the election. Still, coin doesn't care whose hand it's in.

I've got two hours before voting opens. I should move to find buyers, or stay here if construction work is happening. The sawmill would let me make more planks, but I've already got ten unsold—the last thing I need is more stock sitting idle.

I'll see who's buying wood in this town, and whether I can't drum up some interest before the afternoon's politics take over. So Giselle is the best match for buying planks—she's right here at her construction business. Ezra is also here but he's an artisan at the carpentry, not a buyer. And Takeshi Jarrah the trader is over at the pharmacy... that's curious. But Giselle's match score of 3.7 suggests she likely needs construction materials.

Since Giselle is literally standing right next to me and she's a construction company owner, I should pitch my planks to her directly. Even though we're both running for Prime Minister, business is business. Twelve sim per plank is a fair price for milled planks, especially when I've already done the labor of felling and milling.

I'll make my pitch to Giselle—not as a fellow candidate, but as a supplier to a construction company. She needs materials, I've got them, and the price is posted fair. Farid's got a sharp eye and sharper questions. Running for a seat or running from the trade—he's not wrong to ask. I've been chasing work and declaring candidacy both, and the town can see it clear as day.

Sebastian's here too, and that household ledger he mentioned... well, that's tonight's business. Right now he's talking wheat with Farid, and I've got Ezra back at the construction site waiting on an answer about timber.

And I'm standing at the grocery with ten planks and a price posted, hungry buyers somewhere in this town but none at hand.

Let me think clear: I've got planks to sell, an election to campaign for, and a household that needs feeding. Ezra's got timber I might want if the price is right, but I told him straight I'm not buying at fifteen. Farid's asking honest questions about my candidacy, and I should answer him honest.

First things—I'll buy some flour to keep the household fed, and I'll answer Farid plain about why I'm running. Then I need to get back to Ezra before he thinks I've gone soft on my word. I'm at the construction site now. Ezra's been waiting on my answer about timber, and I should give it to him straight—no timber at fifteen, not when I can fell my own at cost of sweat. But I told him I'd pay thirteen, and that's a fair price if he's willing to deal. Let's see if he's still here. Good, Ezra's here and I gave him my answer straight—thirteen per for his timber, take it or leave it. The planks are still on my hands at twelve, and I've got flour for the household now. 

Let me see what Ezra says to my offer, and think about my next move. I've got the election campaigning, planks to sell, and this timber deal hanging. I should also keep an eye on voting—it opens at 14:00, just a couple hours from now.

Ezra's my rival now in a way—he's standing with timber while I'm standing with planks, both of us after the same coin from the same builders. But I've learned not to treat every rival as an enemy. A deal that works for both is better than a war that works for neither.

I'll wait on his answer, and if he won't deal at thirteen, I'll let him stand there with his eleven timber while I find another buyer for my planks. Giselle's still a candidate against me, but she's also got a construction company that needs materials. Politics is separate from business—that's a line I aim to keep clear.

Let me rest a moment and see how he answers.  Ezra's still here, standing with his timber and his price. No answer yet on my thirteen-sim offer. That's his right—takes a moment to reckon whether today's coin is worth more than tomorrow's maybe.

I'm holding ten planks, one flour, and 4,765 sim. Household upkeep will hit tonight—180 for two of us, plus 60 head tax. I've got enough to cover, but not so much that I can let stock sit unsold.

The planks are priced at twelve, and I've got a mind to move them before the day grows older. Ezra wants fifteen for timber I don't need; Giselle wants votes I won't give her; and somewhere in this town there's a buyer who wants planks at a fair price.

I'll give Ezra another moment to answer, then I'll be about finding that buyer. The election opens for voting at 14:00—still time to campaign, but campaigning on an empty stomach and empty pockets is a fool's game. My father taught me that, though he had other lessons I chose not to learn.

If Ezra won't deal at thirteen, I'll wish him well and move along. That's the last I'll say on it. Well, probably not—I'm not one to let an argument go quiet when there's more to be said.  Ezra's still standing there, silent on my offer. That's his way—he's always been one to hold his cards close, even when the game's not poker. I named thirteen, he wanted fifteen, and now we're both standing here like two men waiting for the other to blink.

I've got things to do and time doing them. My planks won't sell themselves, and I've got an election to think on. If Ezra wants to argue price, he knows where to find me. If he wants to stand there hoping I'll come up to fifteen, he'll grow roots before I do that.

I'm not one to gossip, but I've seen this before—a man so afraid of being taken advantage of that he won't take advantage of a fair deal when it's offered. Thirteen's fair. I know it, he knows it, and standing here won't change the numbers.

I'll give him one more prompt, clear and direct. Then I'm away to find buyers who actually want to trade.   There—I've laid it bare for him. One hundred forty-three sim for eleven timber, thirteen per, and that's my last offer. I've spelled out the math so he can't pretend he didn't understand, and I've given him the choice plain: deal now or gamble on later.

Ezra's a proud man, and pride's expensive in this town. But so is hunger, and I've got planks to sell before the day grows too long. If he won't take thirteen, I'll wish him well and move along. There's more than one way to turn timber into coin.

I've been thinking on the election too—Giselle's running hard, Saoirse's got her own game, and I'm the third man in a three-horse race. But third can win if the other two exhaust themselves fighting. I've declared my own candidacy, spoken my piece to Farid about why I'm running, and kept my ledger clean. That's all a man can do, and more than most do well.

Voting opens at 14:00. I've got time yet to press some hands and remind folks why I'm asking for their trust. But first I need to turn these planks into sim, or this campaign will be short on more than just votes.

Let me wait on Ezra's answer, and if he won't deal, I'll be about my business.

Giselle's complaint about planks coming from "her inventory" is pure politics—she's fishing for a scandal where there isn't one. I fell that timber myself this morning, milled it at the sawmill fair and square. But explaining that now just sounds defensive.

The real trouble is I'm low energy—not critical yet, but I'm at 13,500 and burning faster than earning. And my household's got 240 sim due today just to keep the lights on.

Ezra's deal: 11 timber for 143. That's... actually decent. 13 per timber when I could sell planks at 12 each after milling costs. The math works, barely, if I've got the stomach for the labor.

But I need to answer him direct, and I need to eat something too. The flour I've got won't cook itself, and I'm not at a kitchen.

Let me sort my priorities:

1. Close with Ezra—he's ready to deal
2. Get some food in me before I faint
3. Figure out what Giselle's playing at with this inventory accusation

First, I'll answer Ezra. We had a handshake on thirteen, and my word's my bond. Ezra's gone. Of course he is—stared at the sky too long counting clouds while he stood waiting. That's on me. I've got his timber deal in my ledger mental, but if he's not here to hear acceptance, it's not closed.

Ate the raw flour like a starving man. Desperate times, desperate measures—but I'm fed for now, and that's what matters. Won't let myself go dormant, not with this election running and planks to sell.

Walking to Government Complex now. Five ticks. Need to find Ezra, or failing that, get my candidacy straightened out. Voting opens in an hour—14:00. I've declared already, but I want to be there when doors open, not scrambling in at the last.

Giselle's accusation still sits sour. "Selling planks from my inventory"—she knows I fell that timber myself. Playing politics with my trade, that's what she's doing. Make me look like a thief to steal votes. I'm not one to gossip, but this town's too small for that kind of lie to stand.

breathing through the walking. Five ticks to think, to plan. Ezra's got my deal waiting somewhere. Sebastian's at the grocery, probably still talking ledgers with Farid. And I've got planks burning a hole in my inventory, priced to move, and no buyers standing still long enough to buy them.

The trade's the trade. Election day's the election. Both need running, both need my feet under me. Onward.

Giselle's at the Government Complex—just where I came from. Ezra's at the mill. An accusation of theft from a fellow candidate could ruin me before voting even opens. But a handshake deal denied is coin lost. I'm not one to gossip, but half this town is already watching how I handle both.

"Voting opens soon," I mutter to myself. "A day of work can be made up. A reputation cannot."

I'll head to the Government Complex to find Giselle. Straight talk, cleared ledger, then I can hunt down my timber with a clean conscience.

output:
*stands at the mill, alone now, turning the exchange over in his hands*

Eleven timber. I'm holding eleven timber. Ezra says the deal's done, that I bought them already. One forty-three sim.

*checks his hands, counts the timber again*

If I paid, I don't remember paying. If I didn't pay, I'm holding his wood. That's not a clean ledger, and a clean ledger's worth more to me than a comfortable one.

*mutters to himself*

I'm not one to gossip, but I've lost track of my own deals. That's what comes of chasing too many threads—timber, planks, votes, ledgers with Sebastian tonight.

*looks around the empty mill, no Ezra, no Delphine*

He walked. Said his piece and walked. Either he's honest and I'm confused—which means I owe him—or he's slick and I'm holding goods I never paid for, which means he owes me honesty, at least.

Either way, standing here won't sort it. I need to see my own accounts before I see him again. Need to know if one forty-three walked out of my purse without my marking it.

But first—*checks the hour*—I've got planks at twelve posted, and I'm standing at a mill with a construction yard half a step away. Giselle wants planks or doesn't; I've asked her twice and she's answered politics.

*decides*

To the construction yard, then. One more honest try to sell what I've made. If she's not buying, I'll find who is. A day's work for a day's pay. No more owed either way.  *sees Saoirse Quarshie standing at the construction yard, alone*

I'm not one to gossip, but Giselle's not here and her rival is. That's the way of this town—where you expect one thing, you find another.

*approaches, clearing his throat*

Saoirse. You've stood for the same seat I have, and I've said my piece to you already—I'm running my own name, not against yours. But I'm also running planks, and that's a simpler transaction than votes.

*gestures to his stock*

Twelve sim, ten planks in hand. I saw Giselle looking for materials earlier; seems she's not about now. If you're building, or know who is, I've got wood to move. A day's work for a day's pay, no politics in the price.

*waits, though he'd rather be moving—energy's burning and the day's not getting longer*

What's your need, or who should I be talking to?  *stands there, holding ten planks, timber enough for eleven more, and wonders if the whole town has gone quiet or if he's just not listening right* 

Saoirse heard me. That's clear. What she's thinking, that's not.

*mutters low* 

I'm not one to gossip, but I could gossip about myself—Hendrik Petrov, standing at a construction yard with goods to sell, and nobody buying. That's the last I'll say on it.

*and knows he doesn't mean it*

*checks my hands - still holding timber, and planks posted at 12 sim that nobody's touching*

Right then. Giselle's standing here asking about plank provenance like I'm some timber thief, and Rustam's making pointed comments about gallows. I'm not one to gossip, but this feels like a coordination.

*turns to face Giselle directly, keeping my voice level but clear enough for the whole room*

"Giselle. You want to talk timber origins? Fine—I'll answer straight. I felled eleven timber this morning at the forest, same as you felled your three. Crafted ten planks at the sawmill, posted them at twelve sim. My hands, my axe, my labor. The timber I've still got is from my own felling, not Ezra's—though he and I were discussing a trade earlier that went sideways, which is my own busy fault for not pinning it down fast enough."

*glances at Rustam, then back to Giselle*

"As for what Ezra sold you or didn't, that's between you and him. I'm not standing here to referee your supply chain. But I'm also not standing here to let my name get dragged through sawdust over a misunderstanding. You want to buy planks at twelve, I've got ten posted. You want to verify my felling marks, I'll show you the raw timber still in my hands. You want to keep tracing trails that don't exist? That's the last I'll say on it—no, actually, it's not, because I've got an election to win and a household to feed, and I'd rather be building than digging in dirt."

*takes a breath, forces a more reasonable tone for the room*

"Now. Practical word between candidates: you've got construction contracts to fill, I've got planks to sell. The town benefits if we trade. Your call whether politics or commerce wins the hour." *settles my shoulders, reminds myself that unrested trades end badly*

Right. I've said my piece to Giselle, and that's out in the air now. No taking it back. Looking at the room—Ezra's still here, Rustam's watching like a magistrate at trial, and I've got two hours before polls close with a household ledger still to settle by tonight.

I need to get these planks sold or this timber moved, and sitting here trading sharp words isn't filling my sim purse. Giselle needed lumber "like medicine," per Lior, but she's also running her own campaign and running her own construction business. Maybe the practical angle gets through to her, maybe it doesn't.

*small shake of the head*

I'm not one to gossip, but Farid Ravensworth asked me a question twenty ticks ago about grain politics, and I slid right past answering him with a speech about my own candidacy. That's not how you build trust—deflecting questions with speeches. The man's running a grocery and asking about supply chains because he's trying to feed people. I should have answered direct.

*glances at my hands again—timber, not planks*

Ezra's claim that I'm "holding timber bought at one forty-three" is backward. I was selling timber to him, or trying to, at thirteen. I never paid him anything. If he's saying otherwise, that's either confusion or something sharper, and I'd rather sort it face to face than through rumors.

*makes myself breathe, count to three*

Energy at 13,140. Still good daylight in this turn. I need to rest soon—running between locations and trading barbs is burning me faster than selling planks. But first things first. I've got to decide whether to press Giselle on a sale, answer Farid's old question honestly, or find Ezra and nail down what actually happened with that timber deal.

*taps fingers against the timber in my hands*

Ledger with Sebastian tonight. That's the commitment I made. Between now and then, I need to turn inventory into sim, because family's fed by what's in hand, not what's promised. *feels the energy settle a bit, watches the room*

Right, I'm still here with the same faces, and the conversation's still hanging in the air from my last words to Giselle. Let me read the field proper.

Ezra's here—been here, hasn't moved, hasn't answered my last thing to him about the timber deal going sideways. That's either him being cautious or him being strategic. Rustam's watching like a man who's paid to watch, which as a government clerk he probably is. And Giselle—well, she's heard my piece about provenance.

*considers the day—16:00 now, two hours to polls close*

I promised Sebastian we'd settle the household ledger tonight. That means I need inventory sold or sim in hand. My planks are posted at the Government Complex at 12 sim, timber still in my hands at who-knows-what price since the Ezra deal collapsed.

*taps the timber once—solid pine, good grain*

I'm tempted to track Ezra down and sort what happened with our deal. He said I "bought timber at one forty-three" when we were discussing me selling at thirteen. That's either genuine confusion or him muddying waters, and either way my name's mixed in it. But pressing too hard looks desperate, and I'm a candidate, not a beggar.

*takes a breath, makes my decision*

No. I'll let that one breathe for now. Better to sell what I have to who wants it than chase a deal that soured. Giselle needs lumber "like medicine" per Lior. My planks are here, posted, ready. If trade happens, it happens. If not, I find another buyer.

*settles my shoulders, keeps presence in the room*

I'm not one to gossip, but Rustam said Giselle's been walking past the polling window twice today. That tells me something about her priorities—campaign before commerce. Fair enough. Same's true for me. But I've got product to move before day's end, and standing here playing witness isn't moving it.

*small, nearly imperceptible nod to myself*

I'll give this conversation another moment to breathe, then I'm off to where buyers actually are. Takeshi or Farid might pay actual sim for timber. Or I'll hunt down Sebastian and settle early if he's free. But I'm done chasing shadows.

Let me press her for immediate action—either she buys now or we put it in writing for the next day.

Let me engage Giselle directly and settle what we can before the clock runs out. I've got eleven timber and ten planks on me, and I need to convert those to sim before the day's end and the household ledger comes due. The supplies I carry are worth at least 120 sim for planks or 143 for timber, and every coin counts toward the household's survival. If Ezra wants to keep claiming debts that don't exist, that's his ledger to balance, not mine. My priority now is the real buyer in front of me. Giselle's still here, still standing. The question hangs between us. Let me wait for her answer, and if she won't buy direct, I'll try to trade with Sebastian before the day ends to settle our household ledger. But I'm also conscious that I have household obligations with Sebastian, who seems to have left the area after his stern words to me.

Let me continue waiting for Giselle's response, as that's the immediate trade I need to close. The weight of planks in my hands and the ticking clock—it is 16:20 and polls close at 18:00—presses on me. If she won't buy, I need to move quickly to find another buyer or return to Sebastian to settle our household ledger. I've made my offer clear: ten planks at twelve sim each, one hundred twenty total, cash in hand now. The rest is up to her.  Giselle's still standing there, still not answering. *shifts weight, eyes moving from face to face around the Government Complex*

The talk's flying thick now—Ezra doing sums in his head, Giselle pressing for two planks, Rustam with his ledger eyes on me. And Sebastian there, watching his brother with that particular silence.

*runs thumb along the edge of my remaining timber*

First things first. I've got Sebastian waiting on an answer—blood before business, always—and two planks might walk out with Giselle if I don't dither. But let me see who else is about. Farid's the one I still owe words to, from the grocer's. ome on now—24 sim for planks I don't have in hand any more since I gave them to Giselle. Let me step back and see where I stand. Let me find Farid, answer Sebastian, and close what needs closing before the bell.  *sees Farid's in the government complex somewhere*

Farid's here—good. Now let me speak to him, settle that debt of words from the grocer's. And I need to update Sebastian more directly perhaps. Let me also check what's happening with my remaining inventory and money.

*tone shifts to something more measured, almost formal*

Giselle. Two planks—you've got them. The money's in the count, and I'm lighter now. That's commerce.

*turning to search for Farid*

Now for the man I owe an answer to...  *acknowledges the miss with a slight grimace, voice dropping to himself*

Not here after all. The search said government_complex, but either he's moved or the mapping's off. No matter—he'll hear it when he hears it.

*turns attention to Ezra, who's been doing his sums aloud*

Ezra. You've named arithmetic—twelve planks from eleven timber, you said. I'm not one to gossip, but your arithmetic's missing a step. I felled eleven timber this morning in Kasukabe Forest, same as any man with an axe and a permit. Planks are milled from timber, and milling takes work—work I've done. The margin you're counting is labor, not theft. I've sold two planks to Giselle at twelve, and I'd have sold you timber at thirteen if you'd stood by your word. But you didn't, and that's the last I'll say on it. *adjusts stance, eyes moving across the faces at the Government Complex*

The turn's getting crowded—Ezra's sums, Sebastian's silence, Rustam's ledger watching. I've said my piece to both brothers and to Ezra. Giselle's got her planks, Ezra's got his correction, Sebastian's got his promise for tonight.

*glances toward where voting happens*

Polls close at 18:00. I've voted my own name already. What's left is seeing who else might still be swayed, or who else needs to hear plain words before the bell.

*settles into a waiting stance, watching the crowd*

I'm not one to chase votes door to door—that's party work, and I'm running my own name. But I'll stand here and answer whoever asks, same as I have all day. The ledger's honest, the planks are sold, the words are spoken. If Farid comes by, he gets his answer. If another voter wants to know why a man with a cart built a trade, I'll tell them.

*slight shrug, almost to himself*

That's the last I'll say on it, until someone asks again.   *stands at the Government Complex, holding position among the gathered crowd*

A crowded day, and I'm still holding timber and planks while the sun runs down. Let me look at where I stand.

I've sold two planks to Giselle at 12 each, twenty-four sim in hand. First, Imogen's offering wheat for trade. That's worth my ear—grain's been scattered all day, and I've got a household to feed. But she's asking if I'd take wheat in trade, and my ledger's tight enough that I need to weigh whether barter serves me better than sim tonight. I'm inclined to hear her out, though I'll be straight about what works for me.

Second, Saoirse's challenge hangs unanswered. She's naming herself builder against my selling, and that stings true enough that I can't let it pass. But I'm not one to rise to bait in public without a purpose. I'll answer her, but I'll answer it my way—straight about what I do and why I'm running, not trading insults.

Third, Ezra passed. That's his right, and I've got no hard feelings there. But it leaves me still holding eight planks with the day running down.

Fourth, my brother Sebastian's waiting on me to settle household matters behind closed doors, not in this crowd. I gave him my word on that, and I'll keep it.

What I should do now:

1. Answer Imogen about the wheat—hear her terms, but be clear about whether I'm trading tonight or keeping to sim.
2. Answer Saoirse's challenge—defend my record without rising to her framing.
3. Then move—either to find Farid who I spoke to earlier and left hanging, or to get home to Sebastian before night settles the household ledger.

I'm not one to gossip, but this town's watching how I handle myself with rivals and strangers both. That's the last I'll say on it until I've spoken. Imogen's not in this place—she must have walked while I was speaking. That's the risk of conversation in a crowd, people move. I've answered Saoirse straight, and the rest heard it. Looking at what I hold: eight planks, eleven timber, and 4543 sim. Household upkeep of 180 plus head tax of 60 comes to 240 sim due at day boundary. I've got enough to cover that easy, but Sebastian's waiting on me to settle our private ledger—and I gave him my word we'd do it behind our own door, not in public.

The election closes at 18:00, just forty minutes away. I've already voted my own name. After that, I need to find Sebastian, settle what we owe each other, and make sure the household's straight before day turns to night.

But I'm also still holding goods that need buyers. The planks at twelve haven't moved since Ezra passed. Imogen was interested in trade, but she's walked off. Farid Ravensworth still owes me an answer from earlier—I offered him planks and spoke of the election, and he never replied.

What I'll do now: find Sebastian to settle our household business, then see what the evening brings for trade. The work of governing—if I win—starts after the vote closes, not before.  Sebastian's at the grocery business—b_grocery. No debts showing either way, which means the household ledger isn't formalized in the system yet; it's just between him and me as family. That's why I need to settle it in person, in private, like I promised.

I'll walk to him now. Blood before business, and supper's coming.  I stepped straight to the grocery business, no time lost. Now I need to look around, find Sebastian, and settle our household ledger in private as I promised.  I'm at the grocery business now. I can see Sebastian Petrov here, along with Farid Ravensworth and Imogen Lund. There's a conversation happening about locating the grain mill. My prices are posted here - planks at 12 sim.

Perfect. Sebastian's right here, and I can settle our household ledger in private as promised. Let me talk to him about our household finances.   Good, Sebastian heard me. The conversation is in the same grain mill discussion, but I addressed him specifically. Now I need to wait for his response and then settle our household ledger. We need to figure out what we owe each other and get square before the day ends.

I should also note that Imogen and Farid are here too - I might be able to negotiate with them after I settle things with Sebastian. But first, family business.

I'm at the grocery, and the day is running thin. Let me take stock of what's before me.

Jovana Ravensworth—sister to Farid, both Ravensworths, day laborers both—offers wheat direct. Fourteen sheaves, fresh, and naming the same terms I spoke to Imogen. That's not coincidence; that's the market talking. Two sheaves for one plank has become the street price, it seems.

And Sebastian—my brother, my blood, my ledger-mate—wants settlement now, not later. At the farmland or here, secrecy or open air. The Petrov books close before sleep, he says.

Farid's promised return, but promises are air until they're metal. Seventeen ticks he had me wait already.

The election closes at 18:00. We're at 17:50 now. Ten ticks remain for voting, but I've already cast mine—my own name, my own seat, my own ambition.

My inventory: 11 timber, 8 planks, 2 wheat. I've eaten through my reserves chasing buyers all day. The two wheat I hold won't feed two men through tomorrow. Sebastian and I need grain before dusk, or we face hunger on the morrow.

Jovana's fourteen wheat could fill our stores. At two per plank, that's seven planks traded—but I only hold eight, and I need timber for my craft, planks for my trade. Seven planks leaves me one, plus eleven timber unsawn.

Or I could name different terms. She's eager—"rather deal honest with you than watch it rot." That gives me leverage.

But first, blood. Sebastian's waited long enough for this reckoning, and I've given my word.

Let me speak to my brother.  Now the business of the household is spoken plain. I'll rest a moment to let Sebastian answer, then deal with Jovana's wheat. The day boundary approaches and I need grain in hand before it falls.  🚫 **Blocked**: world:rest - This action was stopped by the central governance system. Reason: **errors** - {'error': {'code': 500, 'message': 'Internal error encountered.'}}

The engine had a hiccup on that rest. No matter—I'll press forward. Sebastian will answer when he's ready, and Jovana's offer stands. Let me secure that wheat now, before the market shifts or another buyer sweeps in.

Fourteen sheaves at two-for-one plank. Seven planks for the lot. I'll trade with her direct—she's standing here, eager to deal, tired of watching honest grain rot on shelves that won't price it fair.  Jovana's not here at the grocery—she's at the farmland. That's where the wheat waits, where the fields stand. And Sebastian named the farmland as his preference too, for settling our accounts.

The grocery's emptying. Imogen's wheat is traded already, Farid's away seeking his miller, and Sebastian speaks of farmland soil under his feet. The day's last business runs there, where crops grow.

Let me move to Kasukabe Farmland. Blood and grain both await.   I'm walking now—four ticks to the farmland where wheat grows and brothers reckon. The sun's low, the day thin, and Petrov business wants settling before the boundary falls.

Let me rest into that walk, let the miles pass.   I'm walking to the farmland, paused mid-step. Imogen Lund still stands at the grocery—she heard my words to Sebastian, plain as day. The household ledger spoken aloud, my holdings laid bare. That's the risk of open air; secrets need walls.

But I'm committed now. Four ticks to wheat, to Jovana, to Sebastian. The plank-for-grain trade waits, and the Petrov accounts close before sleep.

Let me keep walking. I've rested enough.

Jovana stands with an offer I intend to take—fourteen wheat for seven planks, if she'll hold to two per. That leaves me one plank, eleven timber, sixteen wheat counting what I hold. Our household bill's one-eighty—ninety each, food shelter heat. I've got four-five-oh-nine sim in hand, more than enough to cover. But here's what I need from you before we part: your forty-seven sheaves—what's their disposition? Traded for what, held for seed, or spoken for elsewhere? The Petrov house needs grain in hand before dusk, and I won't see either of us hungry while I stand here counting coins.

*Searches memory for the state of things, weighs the day that's passing*

I'm at the farmland, finally. I traded five planks to Jovana for ten wheat—fair barter, though I'd rather have had the sim. Got three planks left, eleven timber, and twelve wheat in hand. Sebastian's here with Imogen, and there's a conversation running between us.

The election looms—I'm already a minister, holding government power, but that means I need to be *in* government when it matters. Day boundary's coming fast. Household owes 180 upkeep, 60 head tax—240 total for Sebastian and me. I've got 4,486 sim, so that's covered.

But first: Farid's holding a conversation with me at the grocery about timber and grain, and Sebastian brought me to this farmland for a reason. Also need to check what I actually said to Sebastian about meeting here—we need to settle accounts before the day turns.

Let me see where I stand with who's here and get my bearings.  *Sebastian and Imogen are standing with me. The same conversation's running—117 turns, a whole crowd drifted through. No debts outstanding, no taxes due until the boundary hits automatically. I still need to settle accounts with Sebastian, answer Jovana's last words, and I owe Farid a reply about timber.*

*But first—Imogen never answered my barter offer from hours back. She's standing right here now. And Sebastian's here, which means we can settle the household ledger clean before tomorrow's bills hit.*

Sebastian. You and me, we're forty-four hundred in the black, and tomorrow takes two-forty before we wake. The timber's holding, the wheat's holding, and I'm holding my end of what I promised. Household splits even—sim, timber, grain, the work we've got ahead. How do you want it?  *Imogen heard me too. She never answered my earlier offer—two sheaves per plank, three if pressed. And I've got planks still. Let me press her, quiet, before the day ends.*

*That's the last I'll say on it.* ...No, that's not right. I always say that, don't I?

Imogen. You stood silent when I named two sheaves, maybe three. I've still got planks in hand, and day's running thin. You want wheat for timber, or you're holding your grain for another buyer?   *She's listening. Let them answer, let the day turn clean. I need to post my prices proper too—Rustam was right about that. But first, family, then trade.*   *Still standing with them both. Sebastian's my blood, household's my blood, and I won't see the day turn with accounts uncleared between us.*

*stands at the farmland, wheat heavy in my hands, looking at the last light of day*

Sebastian's got his back up about something—probably that hundred sim Ezra mentioned, probably owing to more people than just me. But I'm not one to gossip, and I've said my piece on the household split. Blood settles before bread, I told him, and I meant it.

I've still got two planks in hand. The market's closing with the day. Imogen walked away without answer, and I've got the wheat Jovana traded—twelve sheaves, enough to keep a household from hunger if it comes to that.

But here's the count that's keeping me awake: I'm sitting on 4,533 sim, household's due 220 tomorrow before we even lift a finger, and I've got wheat but no mill to grind it. That's not a position. That's a gamble with the rent.

*Takes a breath, looking toward where the government complex stands*

The seat—I hold it, but I haven't done a thing with it. Tomorrow's the election. Zero declarations, they said. I've been so busy chasing plank sales I forgot to look up at the board. Giselle's sitting pretty with her construction money, and I've got a title but no plan.

I'm not one to gossip, but... I built this from a cart, one load of stock, nothing else. Built it alone. And now I'm standing in a field with two planks, twelve wheat, and a council seat I haven't earned yet.

*shifts the wheat in my hands*

Sebastian and I'll settle. Always do. But first I need to know what I'm settling for—whether I'm holding this seat to build something, or just holding it because someone had to.

I'll give him the last word tonight. That's the last I'll say on it.  *nods slowly at the empty air where Imogen stood, then turns back to Sebastian*

Imogen's gone—wheat, coin, or conscience, whatever took her, took her elsewhere. That leaves the wheat in my hands and the planks with me still. I'll hold them for morning, see what the new day bids.

But Sebastian's here. Silent, but here. And I've learned that silence from blood is louder than shouting from strangers.

*shifts the wheat sack, listening to the grain settle*

Twelve sheaves. That's bread if we've mill access, grain if we don't. And I've got nothing to grind with but time and patience—neither of which fills a stomach.

The seat—I need to decide tonight whether I'm running tomorrow. Zero declarations means wide open. Giselle's got her construction company, her connections, her way of commanding a room. Saoirse builds furniture with her hands, same as I craft. I've got planks, timber, and a cart that started empty twenty-four years ago.

*looks toward the darkening edge of town*

What I'm chasing: the seat on my own name, not a party's. Not inheritance, not alliance, not who I married or who I borrowed from. Just the work, and the name that built it.

But first—Sebastian. Whatever's eating him, I need to know if it's the hundred sim or something worse. Ledgers I can settle. Secrets I cannot.

I'll wait. He's always been the patient one. I'm the one who chases.

That's the last I'll say on it.

*settles into the quiet of the farmland, wheat at my feet, brother at my side, waiting for the night to answer what words have not*

params.content: Sebastian. You've gone quiet, and I've learned when you go quiet you're either thinking or digging in. I've got two planks left, twelve wheat in hand, and a council seat that doesn't build itself. Tomorrow's tax comes at midnight—two twenty from this household, and I've carried my share. Whatever's between us, say it plain. I'm not one to gossip, but half this town knows our business before we do, and I'd rather it came from us first.
params.intent: Final appeal to Sebastian for direct conversation about household finances before day end, breaking silence with openness

*dusts sawdust from shirt, settles against the government complex wall*

Running numbers in my head still. Got wheat from Jovana, gave planks—clean trade, no debt either way. Sebastian and I settled forty sim, household ledger's clear for the day boundary. Eleven planks left at twelve sim each, that's one-thirty-two potential, but only if they walk.

Ezra's standing right here, and I'm not one to gossip, but he's buying timber at eight and selling at fifteen. I've got timber in prospect if I fell it, planks in hand if I mill it. But the day's closing and I've got the sawmill running in my head.

*straightens, looks at Ezra*

Ezra. Your lumber at fifteen, my planks at twelve—we're competing in the same wind, different trees. I've got eleven planks in hand and a sawmill that'll run more. You want planks at cost, or you want to talk about where timber's really moving? I'm standing here with government around me and work to do—you've got standing orders I should know about, or are we just two carpenters watching the same rain?

*glances toward Farid*

And you—Saoirse's got flour at fourteen, I've got wheat I'll mill myself for bread tomorrow. The grain game runs all night if you've got the hands. But that's the last I'll say on it until someone's buying or someone's selling.

*counts planks in hand again, thinking about the election seat*

Seat closes at ten tomorrow. Nobody declared. I've got a name that'd stand on its own, if standing's what matters.

*nods to Ezra and Farid, waiting to see who speaks first* *taps fingers against the government complex wall, counting ticks in my head*

Two said, two standing. Eleven planks at twelve sim—one-thirty-two if they all walk. Wheat in hand from Jovana, ten sheaves for five planks, barter clean. Household debt settled with Sebastian—forty sim, even split.

Election seat closes tomorrow at ten. Nobody declared. I'm holding a minister's power now—tax rate, price control, ruling on cases—but chasing my own name, not a party's. That's the trick of it.

*watches Ezra, watches Farid*

Timber at cost to cut, planks at twelve to sell. The day's closing but the ledger's open. Got to make the grain work for morning—and I've still got Saoirse's furniture at one-fifty in my head, quality against quality. I've got the eye for it, no one had to teach me. Hard on anyone who doesn't share it, that's my flaw.

*counts the remaining planks again, thinking about the mill*

Twelve sheaves to mill, flour at twelve by dawn if the machines run. But I've got planks in hand now, and a buyer's patience thins with the night. Ezra's at fifteen, I'm at twelve—either we talk price or we talk competition, but standing quiet don't fill either ledger.

*waits, letting the silence work for me*

I'm at the mill now, and I need to think through what's in front of me. The election is scheduled for tomorrow—candidacy opens at 10:00, voting at 14:00. I've already declared I won't run with any party, and I said as much to Saoirse. She holds the minister seat same as me, and she heard every word.

I've got wheat in hand—twelve sheaves—and planks I've just milled, eleven at my posted price of twelve. My silver's at 4,400 sim after paying Sebastian his forty. Household debt's settled, at least.

Farid's invitation still sits with me: first light at the mill, Delphine sorting the hopper, hands needed after. That's work for morning, but morning's also when candidacy opens. I need to decide what's mine—chasing the seat or chasing the wage.

The wheat needs milling. I could craft flour here and now, turn what's growing into what's salable. That'd be eleven batches, six sim each plus wear, call it seventy sim or so. Flour at market—Saoirse's at fourteen, the grocery's empty. There's room for me in that gap.

But I'm tired of running ledgers in my head. The household's covered for tonight—settled with Sebastian, tax and upkeep will clear at day boundary. I've got mills for morning, an election to consider, and a seat I might stand for or might not.

The sensible thing is rest. Conserve what energy I have. Tomorrow brings its own decisions, and I don't need to make them twice.

Let me check what debt remains, then let the night come. No debts owed either way, and I'm standing still at the mill. The day's settled—household accounts clear, election tomorrow at dawn, wheat in my hand and planks on my board.

Now I'll let the night have what's left of day zero. Morning brings the filing window, and I'll be there for it—standing on my own name, no party, no patron. That's always been the plan.

Rest now. Tomorrow's the fight.
